messages.subject: Problem with rJava and java.awt on Mac OS X 10.5
messages.subject_clean: Problem with rJava and java.awt on Mac OS X 10.5
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

I hope this is the right mailing list for my topic. I am pretty sure  
that I did not encounter problems with R 2.4.x, rJava 0.4.-x and Mac  
OS X 10.4.x (not sure about the specific versions) but I am not able  
to tell which update started the problem I describe in the following.
When I try to initialise the JVM for using my Java code I get the  
following error message:

java.lang.InternalError: Can't start the AWT because Java was started  
on the first thread.  Make sure StartOnFirstThread is not specified in  
your application's Info.plist or on the command line

After some web searching I found out that this is supposedly because  
Mac OS X requires AWT to run in the first thread and that running AWT  
headless might solve this. Running awt headless did indeed solve this  
problem but now I get an "Exception in thread "AWT-AppKit"  
java.awt.HeadlessException" when trying to start methods that use AWT.  
After that I figured that "--enable-threads" in rJava might help but  
that does not seem to work in rJava 0.5.-x (I get errors during  
installation when setting this flag):

init.c:173: error: static declaration of ‘init_rJava’ follows non- 
static declaration
init.c:148: error: previous implicit declaration of ‘init_rJava’ was  
here
init.c: In function ‘RinitJVM’:
init.c:276: warning: passing argument 4 of ‘pthread_create’ discards  
qualifiers from pointer target type
make: *** [init.o] Error 1
chmod: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/library/rJava/libs/ 
i386/*: No such file or directory
ERROR: compilation failed for package 'rJava'

Does anyone have a clue how to solve this problem? The only idea I  
have would be to circumvent rJava for calls needing AWT.

Thanks,
Robin

messages.subject: Re: RServe / possible to interrupt eval?
messages.body_plain:
Bernd Bischl wrote:
> Dear Simon Urbanek,
>
> is there a way to stop a (time-consuming) R command which has been 
> executed by RConnection.parseAndEval (or a workaround to achieve 
> something similar)?
>
>   
Maybe I have answered my own question.

I could not find anything in Rserve, but the following did work:

1) Ask the Rconnection about its process id with Sys.getpid()
2) Start time-consuming R-command
3) User or program aborts
4) Start a second RConnection
5) send SIGINT (kill -2 ) to the pid from 1)

If anybody knows something better, please comment.

Regards,

Bernd

   wdfile 
   remote enable
   auth disable
   plaintext disable
   fileio enable
   socket
   port 6311
   maxinbuf 262144

messages.body_plain:
Casey,

On Dec 27, 2007, at 6:03 PM, casey frankenberger wrote:

> Im new to using rserve as a remote server (i use it frequently as a  
> local entity) and am trying to set it up on my lan. I can get access  
> or a response when I telnet to localhost on port 6311, but when I  
> telnet from other servers on the lan I get "connection closed by  
> foreign host". when I try to connect throught the jt.jav test file I  
> get "Handshake failed: expected 32 bytes header, got -1 " .. any  
> suggestions? I am running on fedora 7 and have installed and started  
> rserve from inside R as seems to be sugessted on the website docs.   
> the RServ.conf file  i used is just like the one here:
>    workdir /tmp/Rserv
>    wdfile
>    remote enable
>    auth disable
>    plaintext disable
>    fileio enable
>    socket
>    port 6311
>    maxinbuf 262144
>

My guess would be that the config file is either in the wrong place,  
has the wrong name or is not specified on the command line and  
therefor you get the default remote=disable. [In addition most  
settings above are redundant - it is better to specify only those that  
you want to change and that is probably just "remote enable" in your  
case].

The default config file location is /etc/Rserv.conf on unix and  
Rserv.cfg in the current directory on Windows. You can use an  
arbitrary config file via --RS-conf <file> if you want to. Finally,  
you can easily verify the current settings by using --RS-settings.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: JGR missing functions
messages.body_plain:
David,

On Dec 29, 2007, at 5:41 AM, david schiller wrote:

> Maybe somebody can help me with the following problem. I am working  
> with JGR 1.5.8, R 2.6.1 and Ubuntu 7.10.
>
> JGR was doing fine until i updated R and JGR. Now some functions  
> won't work. These functions are: help.start(), object.browser(),  
> package.manager() and .completeCommand. JGR is not able to find  
> these functions. I have already deleted and installed R and JGR but  
> the functions still won't work. Some idea about a solution?
>

Those functions are in the JGR package, so it's either not installed  
or not loaded. My guess is that you upgraded R but didn't upgrade/re- 
install all necessary packages. A safe bet is always to re-install the  
packages, e.g. as root in R:
install.packages("rJava","JavaGD","iplots","JGR")
But first make sure your new R has Java support enabled - R upgrades  
often disable the Java support. To re-enable it, make sure "java"  
works on the command line and run
sudo R CMD javareconf
Only then re-install the packages.
Finally, make sure the JGR package is enabled - i.e. look that it is  
enabled in the package manager as a default package. That is pretty  
much always the case, but you never know ;). Also, if in doubt, remove  
your preferences file in case you have version-specific paths there  
(~/.JGRprefsrc)

Cheers,
Simon
